summary: First test run of School OS foundation. Backend pytest suite: 23/24 passed (95.8%). All auth, tenant isolation, RBAC, audit, platform admin, and error envelope tests pass. One CRITICAL security bug found: brute-force lockout is bypassable through the public ingress because the lockout identifier is built from the entire X-Forwarded-For header string (which includes rotating intermediate proxy IPs from Cloudflare/GCP), so each attempt is counted under a different key. Verified: locally on 127.0.0.1 lockout works (429 on 6th), but through the ingress 20+ consecutive failed logins never trigger 429. Frontend: 100% of flows pass (landing, register-school, /school console with 8 module cards, Users tab create-teacher via UI, superadmin login to /platform with tenants-table, cross-role redirect from /school to /platform, logged-out /platform redirects to /login).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout is bypassable via the public ingress. auth_routes.py:147 uses `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')` as the raw string; ingress adds rotating intermediate proxy IPs (e.g. '34.16.56.64,172.70.126.86,34.36.184.211'), so every attempt gets a different identifier and MAX_ATTEMPTS is never reached. Fix: take only the first (leftmost, client) IP via `xff.split(',')[0].strip()` before building `identifier`. Same issue exists in services/audit_service.py:24 (audit IP field will also record noisy chains).

action_items: Fix brute-force IP parsing in /app/backend/app/api/v1/auth_routes.py (login) and /app/backend/app/services/audit_service.py: parse X-Forwarded-For as `xff.split(',')[0].strip()` so lockout counter and audit IP field use the true client IP.
critical_code_review_comments: X-Forwarded-For handling is naive in both auth_routes.py and audit_service.py — always take leftmost IP, not the raw header string.
auth_routes.py:104 duplicate-owner-email check is unreachable (tenant just created is empty); harmless but dead code.
school_routes.py cross-tenant GET returns 404 which is correct (does not leak existence). Good.
Error envelope, cookie flags (httpOnly+Secure+SameSite=None), bcrypt hashes (verified via API round-trip), and refresh-token revocation on logout all behave correctly.

Only the brute-force lockout test is expected to fail until the X-Forwarded-For parsing is fixed. After fix, rerun `pytest backend/tests/test_foundation.py -v`. Frontend flows all pass; use data-testids listed in the request. Note: MongoDB accumulates test tenants across runs — that is fine because tests always use unique random slug suffixes.
rca of the issue: Root cause: request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') returns the entire XFF chain string. On the public ingress the middle hop (Cloudflare edge PoP or GCP load balancer) is not stable — each request may traverse a different edge IP — so the string 'clientIP, edgeIP, lbIP' varies. The lockout key `f'{xff}:{email}'` therefore mutates every request, spreading attempts across many DB rows and never reaching MAX_ATTEMPTS=5. Reproduction: curl the login endpoint 6+ times through the preview URL with wrong password — all return 401, never 429; then query `db.login_attempts` and observe multiple rows for the same email with attempts<5. Mitigation: normalize IP to the leftmost token of XFF (`ip = (xff.split(',')[0].strip() if xff else (client.host or '0.0.0.0'))`) in both auth_routes.py and audit_service.py.
